articles.title: This Is the U.S. Government’s Most Maddening Poverty Trap
articles.dek: Imagine that you’re one of the more than seven million low-income Americans who receive Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, from the federal government. Or maybe you are one of those Americans, in which case you’re all too familiar with the hypothetical story I am about to tell. You have $1,800 in your checking account. But on the last day of the month, a $300 birthday check from your daughter clears, bumping your account to $2,100 as a new month begins. And for that reason alone, you are not eligible for SSI this month. By the next afternoon, that extra $300—or even all $2,100—may be gone.
